messages:
Ingrid: Heads up — noticed p95 on /chat-route (tier: standard) jumped from ~220ms to ~310ms after the kernel-affinity tweak yesterday.
Sam: ack. Which affinity change are we talking about? the matmul prefetch switch?
Ingrid: We switched default kernel to fast_matmul_v2 for medium sequences. KV hit rate dropped from 98% -> 92% on warm traces after the switch.
Noah: 92% KV hit is pretty material. Any correlation with microbatch sizes or token packing?
Ingrid: Yes — average microbatch size fell ~15% (6.8 -> 5.8). Fewer tokens per microbatch, more kernel launches. Profiler shows +12% kernel_launch overhead overall.
Elaine: Did the dynamic token-budget gating change with that rollout? We had a canary that bumped the per-route cap earlier.
Sam: We did roll a small token-cap adjustment: route_token_cap={standard:48,premium:96} but only to a tiny canary. Not sure it should cause this much drop.
Ingrid: Quick profiling snippet pasted: ```trace_summary:
p95=310ms median=60ms avg_batch_tokens=72 avg_microbatch=5.8 kv_hit=0.92```
perf-bot: regression-run 2026-03-18T09:02Z — baseline p95=220ms, current p95=312ms. Top contributors from attribution: kernel_launch_cost (+9%), batch_fragmentation (+6%).
Noah: My working hypothesis: the v2 kernel changes workspace layout -> extra memcpy pattern -> increases per-request setup cost; combined with slightly lowered token packing, that amplifies p95.
Elaine: Two mitigations: (1) short-window coalescing to hold tiny requests up to Xms to get better packing, gated to only standard tier when p95 exceeds threshold; (2) lower the token-floor so small requests can be packed more flexibly.
Sam: I can try token_floor 32->24 in canary. Also revert kernel preference for standard route as a control.
Ingrid: Prototype plan: canary config = {delay_coalesce_ms:8, token_floor:24, kernel_pref:baseline_for_standard}. Will collect kv_hit, avg_microbatch, p95.
Noah: Add a trace flag `X-rt-batch-debug` to force coalesce behavior per-request so we can reproduce without full rollout.
Elaine: Please include full kernel timeline (launch timestamps + duration) in the trace. I'll help wire up profiler sampling for the canary.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: canary/rt-slo-coalesce-20260318 -> 5% traffic at 09:40Z.
Sam: Nice. Acceptance criteria: p95 improvement >10% for standard without degrading premium. If so, roll to 25% then 100%. :thumbsup:
Ingrid: Will run the canary and report back after 30m with numbers and flamegraphs. cc @team-eng-runtime
__notes: single-string thread with short, realistic Slack messages; contains inline code block and bot messages
